blocks.text: Learning securities law becomes easier when each rule has a place. Start with the legal framework, identify the people and businesses involved, then work through registration, duties, exceptions and enforcement.

This interactive study guide turns that structure into a connected reading experience. It brings together 7 chapters, 28 sections, 41 concepts and 66 definitions, with original explanations, applied examples and learning checks.

items.label: Open the Series 63 Study Guide
items.note: Read the chapters, explore related concepts and check your understanding.

blocks.text: The guide follows seven connected questions. Each chapter builds on the earlier ones, while related concepts let you move directly to the rule that explains an exception or a consequence.

items.text: Which law applies, and which authority has the relevant power?
Who is acting, for whom, and in what capacity?
What is being offered, recommended, bought or sold?
Who or what needs registration, and what keeps that status effective?
What must the participant do for the client and the business?
Which requirement changes, under what conditions, and what duties remain?
What happens after a possible violation, and who can take each action?

sections.heading: 02 — Follow the facts through the rules

blocks.text: Maya has sold her business and wants to invest the proceeds. Lucas works with her through Harbor Securities in a brokerage role, or through Cedar Advisory in an advisory role. Northstar Solar is the issuer she encounters along the way. These recurring fictional participants make it easier to see which facts change the analysis.

Change Lucas's capacity, move an office to another state, or give Maya an imminent tax payment. The guide asks how each change affects registration, client care or the available exception. Its 69 original examples connect the concepts to decisions, with checks that explain the reasoning.
Useful distinctions return throughout the material: a firm and its representative, an exempt security and an exempt transaction, disclosure and consent, an administrative order and a court remedy.

Choose Read with a guide to hear each passage and follow its highlight. Practical commentary connects the rules to Maya’s decisions across all 28 sections. Pause, change the pace or begin at a particular section; the explanations are also available to read on the page.

items: Read the chapter to understand where its rules fit. Use the definitions when a term is unfamiliar.
Work through an example and answer the learning check before revealing its explanation.
Follow the related concepts when two rules seem similar. Return to the distinction and explain it in your own words.

blocks.text: This is an original, independent learning project. Links to official sources and dated rule notes help keep the legal framework, state variations and examination context clear as you study.
